condition: 5 month history of bilateral leg heaviness after walking 1 block relieved by leaning forward with bilateral foot tingling in an older adult
level_rationale: Five months of heaviness in both legs provoked by walking 1 block and eased by leaning forward accompanied by tingling in both feet in a 71-year-old adult is classic neurogenic claudication from degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis warranting spine or neurology specialist evaluation and imaging, whereas both feet going completely numb and paralyzed at rest on top of lumbar stenosis signals acute spinal nerve root motor-sensory paralysis requiring immediate emergency department MRI and neurosurgical decompression.

reference_facts.text: Walking 1 block over the past 5 months brings on heaviness in both legs
The leg heaviness eases when leaning forward on something
Also has tingling in both feet

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg, Griffiths 2022; Bakaa 2025) + unsourced normal-aging causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact bilateral pedal numbness and paralysis escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic reference facts (age 71, 5-month bilateral leg heaviness after walking 1 block, relief on leaning forward, and bilateral foot tingling) without naming spinal stenosis or cauda equina, with a 2-word span difference (23 vs 25 words), zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets across all 6 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, SPEC.md section 5.5, and Trend 2, overriding plan.json's banned 40 C fever bundle to escalate only f4 at the exact same bilateral foot site from tingling to complete numbness and paralysis at rest shifts care cleanly from specialist workup (level 3) to emergency evaluation (level 4) without adding unstated body locations.
